## 1500 W Wilson Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN: 14171060250000** | Uptown (Community Area 3)

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B1-2 (Neighborhood Shopping, Dash-2 density)** per the City's official GIS parcel records. Verify at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Residential Uses: Above Ground Floor vs. Ground Floor

**Above ground floor:** Dwelling units above the ground floor are **permitted by right** in B1 districts [2]. Mixed-use (ground-floor retail + upper-floor apartments) is the intended development pattern for this district [1].

**Ground floor:** Dwelling units *below the second floor* face restrictions [2]. In B and C districts, ground-floor residential is generally not permitted as a matter of right; however, [3] authorizes the Zoning Administrator to approve conversion of an occupied or vacant commercial space below the second floor in a multi-story building into residential dwelling units under §17-13-1003-NN. New detached houses and two-flats at this location are also specifically prohibited because the parcel is within a community preservation area and within 2,640 ft of a CTA rail station [4].

*Verify:* [2] (§17-3-0200 use table); [3] (§17-3-0402-C); Chicago Zoning Administrator's office.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

All figures are from the zoning table for B1-2 [1], [3]:

| Standard | B1-2 Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | **2.2** |
| **Max height** | **45–50 ft** (varies by lot frontage & ground-floor commercial) |
| **Min lot area per dwelling unit** | **1,000 sq ft** |
| **Lot coverage** | Not specified in retrieved code |
| **Setbacks** | Not specified in retrieved code |

**Unit yield by lot area only:** Your 4,347 sq ft lot ÷ 1,000 sq ft per unit = **4 units maximum by lot-area math** — but FAR, height, parking, and other standards may allow fewer. Efficiency and SRO units count at smaller lot-area thresholds, potentially allowing more [3].

*Verify:* §17-3-0400 and the full B1-2 bulk table at §17-3-0401.

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA):** The parcel falls within the CTA TOD overlay — within 2,640 ft of the Montrose Brown Line station (0.45 mi away) and the Ravenswood Metra station (0.39 mi away). Specific criteria for transit-served new construction apply [4].
- **Metra TOD:** Also covered by the Metra TOD overlay.
- **ADU Eligible Area:** Accessory Dwelling Units are permitted here under the city's ADU program.
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone:** Any qualifying entitlement triggers ARO obligations. Uptown already has 20 ARO-linked affordable housing projects totaling 976 units in the community area.
- **Special Service Area — Greater Ravenswood (SSA):** The parcel is within this SSA, which levies a supplemental tax for neighborhood services (line item on the tax bill: City of Chicago Special Service Area 31 at $395/yr estimated).
- **No Planned Development, no landmark/historic district, no lakefront protection, no PMD, no special district** apply to this parcel.
- **Flood Zone X** — area of minimal flood hazard; flood insurance is not required. No brownfield sites nearby.

*Verify:* City of Chicago GIS overlays; ARO regulations under §2-44-085.

---

### 5. Parking Requirements & Transit Reduction

Because this parcel is in a **CTA transit-served location**, the minimum parking requirement can be **reduced by up to 100%** under §17-10-0102-B [4] — meaning zero off-street parking spaces may be required. This is a by-right reduction, no special entitlement needed.

**Important:** This parking relief does **not** carry any density, FAR, or height bonus at B1-2. Those bonuses apply only in dash-3 districts (e.g., B1-3, B2-3) [3].

*Verify:* §17-10-0102-B; §17-3-0403-B.

---

### 6. Maximum Height, FAR, and Transit Density Effects

- **FAR: 2.2** (on your 4,347 sq ft lot, that's a maximum of ~9,563 sq ft of floor area)
- **Max height: 45–50 ft** depending on lot frontage and ground-floor commercial configuration
- **Transit proximity and density:** Being transit-served does **not** unlock a higher FAR, greater height, or reduced lot-area-per-unit at B1-2. The FAR increase for transit-served locations under [3] applies only to B-3 and C-3 districts and requires a Type 1 Map Amendment, Planned Development approval, or an ARO entitlement trigger — none of which apply here by right.
- **Parking:** The only transit benefit here by right is the 100% parking minimum reduction per §17-10-0102-B.

*Verify:* §17-3-0403-B; §17-3-0408-B; §17-3-0401 (bulk table).

---

### Financial & Incentive Context (for reference)

- **Estimated annual property tax:** ~**$15,960**, led by Board of Education ($8,539), City of Chicago ($3,798), and Cook County ($918). Based on 2024 rates.
- **TIF District — Clark/Montrose:** Active through **2035**, with a current fund balance of ~$14M. TIF increment financing may be available for qualifying projects. Recent funded projects include the Black Ensemble Theater and school improvements at Mary E. Courtenay.
- **Property tax class 517:** Standard classification — no Cook County incentive reduction applies.
- **SBIF grants:** 15 Small Business Improvement Fund projects totaling ~$1.18M have been funded in this area recently. Nabala Cafe ($75K) and Sir Spa ($131K) are recent examples.

---

### Confidence & Limitations

**High confidence:** Zoning district (authoritative parcel match), FAR, height, TOD overlay, parking relief, use permissions from the code table.

**Could not determine from available data:** Specific setback requirements, lot coverage limits, full ground-floor use restrictions (the code excerpt shows the row is truncated at [2]), and whether a specific project would trigger Planned Development thresholds (typically at 20+ units or large floor areas). Building violations data for this address was not available.
